data structures.task: Review arrays and their time complexities for access, insert, delete
Study linked lists: singly, doubly, and circular variants
Practice stack and queue operations with code examples
Understand binary trees: traversals (in-order, pre-order, post-order)
Learn binary search trees: insertion, deletion, search
Study heaps: min-heap, max-heap, and heap operations
Understand hash tables: collision resolution, load factor
Learn graph representations: adjacency list vs adjacency matrix
Practice BFS and DFS implementations on graphs
Solve 5 data structures problems on LeetCode or GeeksforGeeks

algorithms.task: Review Big O notation and analyze the complexity of common algorithms
Study and implement bubble sort, insertion sort, and selection sort
Implement merge sort and quick sort with detailed trace-through
Practice binary search and its variants (lower bound, upper bound)
Study dynamic programming: memoization and tabulation approaches
Solve classic DP problems: Fibonacci, 0/1 knapsack, longest common subsequence
Learn graph algorithms: Dijkstra's shortest path, Bellman-Ford
Study greedy algorithms and when they give optimal solutions
Complete 10 algorithm problems spanning all topics

operating systems.task: Study OS architecture: kernel, user space, system calls
Learn process vs thread: differences, creation, and lifecycle
Understand CPU scheduling algorithms: FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority
Calculate waiting time and turnaround time for scheduling examples
Study deadlocks: conditions, prevention, detection, and recovery
Understand memory management: paging, segmentation, and virtual memory
Learn page replacement algorithms: FIFO, LRU, Optimal
Study file systems: directory structures, inodes, and FAT
Review inter-process communication: pipes, semaphores, message queues
Practice past exam questions on OS scheduling and memory

database management.task: Review relational model: tables, tuples, attributes, and keys
Study SQL: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
Practice all types of SQL JOINs with example queries
Understand normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF with examples
Study ER diagrams: entities, relationships, cardinality notation
Learn transaction management: ACID properties and isolation levels
Understand indexing: B-tree indexes, clustered vs non-clustered
Study concurrency control: locking protocols and two-phase locking
Review relational algebra operations for query optimization
Solve 10 SQL query problems covering joins, aggregation, and subqueries

computer networks.task: Review the OSI model: all 7 layers, their functions, and protocols
Study the TCP/IP model and compare it to the OSI model
Learn IP addressing: IPv4, subnetting, CIDR notation, IPv6 basics
Understand TCP vs UDP: differences, three-way handshake, flow control
Study routing protocols: RIP, OSPF, and BGP at a conceptual level
Learn HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, and DHCP operation in detail
Understand network security: firewalls, SSL/TLS, and common attacks
Practice subnetting calculations and VLSM problems
Review error detection and correction: CRC, Hamming codes
Solve past exam questions on networking layers and protocols

programming fundamentals.task: Review variables, data types, and operators in your primary language
Study control flow: if-else, loops (for, while, do-while), and switch
Understand functions: parameters, return values, scope, and call stack
Practice recursion: write recursive solutions for factorial, Fibonacci, and power
Study arrays and strings: common operations and built-in methods
Learn about pointers or references depending on your language
Understand exception handling: try, catch, finally, and custom exceptions
Practice OOP: write classes with inheritance and polymorphism
Study file I/O: reading from and writing to files
Solve 15 programming problems covering all fundamentals

mathematics.task: Review sets, relations, and functions: definitions and properties
Study propositional logic: truth tables, logical equivalences
Learn number theory: divisibility, primes, GCD, LCM, modular arithmetic
Understand combinatorics: permutations, combinations, and the pigeonhole principle
Study graph theory: trees, paths, cycles, and Euler/Hamiltonian circuits
Learn recurrence relations and their solutions
Study probability: Bayes' theorem, conditional probability, distributions
Review linear algebra: matrices, determinants, eigenvalues
Practice calculus: differentiation and integration basics
Solve 20 mathematics problems from previous university exam papers

digital electronics.task: Review number systems: binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal conversions
Study Boolean algebra: laws, theorems, and simplification techniques
Learn logic gates: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR with truth tables
Practice Karnaugh map (K-map) simplification for 2, 3, and 4 variables
Understand combinational circuits: adders, subtractors, multiplexers, decoders
Study flip-flops: SR, D, JK, and T flip-flops with timing diagrams
Learn sequential circuits: registers, counters, and state machines
Understand memory devices: ROM, RAM, and cache hierarchy
Solve past exam questions on Boolean simplification and circuit design
